result.answer:
Karnataka — source cutoff: 2026-09-23.

Prototype source review is pending; current availability and individual eligibility are not verified.

- Fast‑charging stations for 2W, 3W, cars and buses receive a capital subsidy of 25 % of the project cost, with a maximum subsidy of Rs 10,00,000 per station, and the policy earmarks up to 500 such stations for incentive support. [S2](https://investkarnataka.co.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Clean-mobility-policy.pdf#page=22)
- Slow‑charging stations are not covered by any incentive; the policy explicitly provides no incentives for slow‑charging stations. [S2](https://investkarnataka.co.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Clean-mobility-policy.pdf#page=22)

observations.question: What lifetime-tax cost slabs and rates for newly registered electric private cars does Part A5(a) of the 2026 Act state?

result.answer:
Karnataka — source cutoff: 2026-09-23.

Prototype source review is pending; current availability and individual eligibility are not verified.

- For newly registered electric private cars (motor cars, jeeps, omni buses and private‑service vehicles) the lifetime tax is a percentage of the vehicle cost: if the cost does not exceed Rs 10 lakh the tax is 5 % of cost; if the cost is more than Rs 10 lakh but does not exceed Rs 25 lakh the tax is 8 % of cost; and if the cost exceeds Rs 25 lakh the tax is 10 % of cost. [S1](https://investkarnataka.co.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Clean-mobility-policy.pdf#page=26) [S2](https://dpal.karnataka.gov.in/uploads/media_to_upload1776323794.pdf#page=6)

Sources:

- [S1: Karnataka — Karnataka Clean Mobility Policy 2025–2030, PDF page 26](https://investkarnataka.co.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Clean-mobility-policy.pdf#page=26)
- [S2: Karnataka — Karnataka Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 2026 — Act 29, PDF page 6](https://dpal.karnataka.gov.in/uploads/media_to_upload1776323794.pdf#page=6)
